#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/common.sh"

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
Usage: beacon-report [--file FILE] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--stale-minutes N]
                     [--conditions FILE]

Print the daily report for the lighthouse network: a count of beacons by
state, every beacon that needs a visit, and the fleet's average battery.

Options:
  --file FILE   status file (default: \$BEACON_STATUS_FILE or data/status.txt)
  --date DATE   date printed in the header (default: today, UTC)
  --stale-minutes N
                minutes of silence before a beacon is stale (default: 30)
  --conditions FILE
                print a Conditions: line per station in FILE, whose lines
                are station|wind|visibility|sea state
  -h, --help    show this help
USAGE
}

file="${BEACON_STATUS_FILE}"
day=""
stale_minutes=30
conditions=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --file) file="${2:?--file needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --date) day="${2:?--date needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --stale-minutes) stale_minutes="${2:?--stale-minutes needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --conditions) conditions="${2:?--conditions needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) usage >&2; exit 64 ;;
    esac
done

[[ "${stale_minutes}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "--stale-minutes must be a whole number"

require_status "${file}"
[[ -z "${conditions}" || -r "${conditions}" ]] || die "cannot read ${conditions}"
now="$(now_epoch)"
[[ -n "${day}" ]] || day="$(date -u -d "@${now}" +%F)"

ok=0 warn=0 fail=0 total=0 battery_sum=0
visits=()

while IFS='|' read -r id name lamp last_seen battery; do
    total=$(( total + 1 ))
    battery_sum=$(( battery_sum + 10#${battery} ))
    seen="$(iso_to_epoch "${last_seen}")"
    age=$(( (now - seen) / 60 ))
    classify_beacon "${lamp}" "${age}" "${battery}" "${stale_minutes}"
    case "${BEACON_STATE}" in
        OK) ok=$(( ok + 1 )) ;;
        WARN) warn=$(( warn + 1 )) ;;
        FAIL) fail=$(( fail + 1 )) ;;
    esac
    if [[ "${BEACON_STATE}" != OK ]]; then
        visits+=("${id} ${name}: ${BEACON_NOTES[*]}")
    fi
done < <(read_status "${file}")

(( total > 0 )) || die "no beacons in ${file}"

printf 'Lighthouse network — daily report for %s\n' "${day}"
printf '%s\n' "================================================"
if [[ -n "${conditions}" ]]; then
    while IFS='|' read -r station wind vis sea; do
        [[ -n "${station}" ]] || continue
        printf 'Conditions: %s — wind %s, visibility %s, sea %s\n' "${station}" "${wind}" "${vis}" "${sea}"
    done < "${conditions}"
fi
printf 'beacons: %d   ok: %d   warn: %d   fail: %d\n' "${total}" "${ok}" "${warn}" "${fail}"
printf 'average battery: %d%%\n' $(( battery_sum / total ))
echo
if (( ${#visits[@]} == 0 )); then
    echo "No visits needed."
else
    echo "Needs a visit:"
    printf '  - %s\n' "${visits[@]}"
fi

Check every beacon in the status file and print one line each:

  OK     lamp lit, heard from recently, battery healthy
  WARN   stale (no report for N minutes) or battery below 20%
  FAIL   lamp reported anything other than "ok"

Options:
  --file FILE         status file (default: \$BEACON_STATUS_FILE or data/status.txt)
  --stale-minutes N   minutes of silence before a beacon is stale (default: 30)
  --quiet             print only beacons that are not OK
  -h, --help          show this help

Exit status: 0 all OK, 1 any WARN, 2 any FAIL, 64 usage error.
USAGE
}

file="${BEACON_STATUS_FILE}"
stale_minutes=30
quiet=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --file) file="${2:?--file needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --stale-minutes) stale_minutes="${2:?--stale-minutes needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --quiet) quiet=true; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) usage >&2; exit 64 ;;
    esac
done

[[ "${stale_minutes}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "--stale-minutes must be a whole number"

require_status "${file}"
now="$(now_epoch)"
worst=0

while IFS='|' read -r id name lamp last_seen battery; do
    seen="$(iso_to_epoch "${last_seen}")"
    age=$(( (now - seen) / 60 ))
    classify_beacon "${lamp}" "${age}" "${battery}" "${stale_minutes}"
    state="${BEACON_STATE}"

    case "${state}" in
        WARN) (( worst < 1 )) && worst=1 ;;
        FAIL) worst=2 ;;

    if [[ "${quiet}" == true && "${state}" == OK ]]; then
        continue
    fi

# shellcheck shell=bash

BEACON_ROOT="$(cd -- "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." >/dev/null && pwd)"
BEACON_STATUS_FILE="${BEACON_STATUS_FILE:-${BEACON_ROOT}/data/status.txt}"
BEACON_LOG_DIR="${BEACON_LOG_DIR:-${BEACON_ROOT}/data/logs}"

die() {
    printf '%s: %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >&2
    exit 64
}

now_epoch() {
    if [[ -n "${BEACON_NOW:-}" ]]; then
        date -u -d "${BEACON_NOW}" +%s
    else
        date -u +%s
    fi
}

iso_to_epoch() {
    date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || die "bad timestamp: $1"
}

require_status() {
    [[ -r "$1" ]] || die "cannot read status file: $1"
}

read_status() {
    local file="$1"
    grep -v -e '^[[:space:]]*#' -e '^[[:space:]]*$' "${file}"
}

# classify_beacon LAMP AGE_MINUTES BATTERY [STALE_MINUTES]
# Sets BEACON_STATE (OK|WARN|FAIL) and BEACON_NOTES (array of reasons).
classify_beacon() {
    local lamp="$1" age="$2" battery="$3" stale="${4:-30}"
    BEACON_STATE=OK
    BEACON_NOTES=()
    if [[ "${lamp}" != "ok" ]]; then
        BEACON_STATE=FAIL
        BEACON_NOTES+=("lamp ${lamp}")
    fi
    if (( age > stale )); then
        [[ "${BEACON_STATE}" == FAIL ]] || BEACON_STATE=WARN
        BEACON_NOTES+=("silent ${age}m")
    fi
    if (( 10#${battery} < 20 )); then
        [[ "${BEACON_STATE}" == FAIL ]] || BEACON_STATE=WARN
        BEACON_NOTES+=("battery ${battery}%")
    fi
}

lastPrompt: Why do these scripts exit 64 on a bad option rather than 1?

content.text:
They're using exit code 64 because it's the standard convention for command-line usage errors. This comes from BSD's `sysexits.h` header, where `EX_USAGE` is defined as 64.

You can see this documented explicitly in `beacon-status` at line 21:

```bash
Exit status: 0 all OK, 1 any WARN, 2 any FAIL, 64 usage error.
```

The `die()` function in `common.sh` (line 9) also exits with 64, which covers argument validation errors like invalid timestamps or missing files.

This is a good convention because it distinguishes usage errors (64) from runtime errors (1), allowing callers to handle them differently if needed.
